item.title: What’s in the New U.S.-Saudi Minerals Agreement?
item.description: The U.S.-Saudi minerals partnership marks a realignment in global supply chains—pairing Saudi Arabia’s vast heavy rare earth reserves with significant U.S. investment to build a mine-to-magnet pathway that directly reduces China’s leverage and strengthens allied security.

item.title: Force Design for the Twenty-First Century Fight: U.S. Cyber Force Lessons from China’s Strategic Support Forces
item.description: As the United States debates the creation of a standalone Cyber Force, it should learn the lessons China’s decade-long Strategic Support Force experiment offers in integrating space, cyber, and information capabilities for a new era of warfare.

item.title: Energy Leverage in the Russia-Ukraine War: Dialogue with Senator Lindsey Graham and Senator Richard Blumenthal
item.description: Senator Lindsey Graham (R-SC) and Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) joined the CSIS Energy Security and Climate Change Program to discuss the intersection of energy and foreign policy in the context of the war in Ukraine

item.title: How to Win the Information Game in Venezuela
item.description: As U.S. strategic interest in Venezuela grows, agentic AI and tailored messaging emerge as critical tools in the information domain—offering influence without escalation.

item.title: Chinese Coercion of Taiwan’s Energy Lifelines: A Contest Taiwan and the West Can’t Afford to Lose
item.description: China’s gray-zone campaign against Taiwan targets its energy lifelines—no war declared, just slow suffocation. A CCP shadow siege threatens not just Taiwan’s grid but the global tech supply chain. The West must act—before exhaustion wins.

item.title: Finding Congress
item.description: This week, Bill Reinsch examines Congress’s role in shaping trade policy and proposes ways for lawmakers to delegate its constitutional powers.

item.title: Power Under Pressure: The Fight to Protect Taiwan’s Energy Lifelines from Beijing’s Aggression
item.description: A panel of experts at FDD examines China’s use of coercive energy tactics against Taiwan, evaluating risks to regional stability and the global supply chain while outlining U.S. policy options to reinforce deterrence and support Taiwan’s energy resilience.
